sections.h2: What does the Macon-Bibb County government do with property tax?
sections.html:
Macon and Bibb County merged into one consolidated government on January 1, 2014, after voters approved the change on July 31, 2012. A mayor elected countywide and a nine-member commission elected by district now run it, and the small city of Payne was folded in during 2015. For property owners that means a single local government, one county school district and one tax commissioner for the whole county.

The Tax Commissioner's office is at 188 Third Street, Macon, Georgia 31201, open 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., with a main line of (478) 621-6500 and an email address of taxinfo@maconbibb.us. The office bills and collects, prepares the tax digest for the state, and passes the money to the State of Georgia, Macon-Bibb County and the school board. Values come from a separate Board of Tax Assessors at (478) 621-6701.

  • Tax Commissioner: statements, payments, liens, tax sales, excess funds claims.
  • Tax Assessors: values, returns, homestead applications, appeal filings.
  • Solid Waste Department: the garbage fee that appears alongside the property bill.

sections.h2: What is the Macon-Bibb housing market like for a seller?
sections.html:
Bibb is the largest county in the Macon metro area, with about 250 square miles of land along the Ocmulgee River. I-16, I-75 and I-475 cross it, and Lake Tobesofkee about 10 miles west of downtown has three county parks. Ocmulgee National Monument preserves Mississippian mound sites along the river. Bibb County School District covers the whole county, and the Macon Transit Authority runs the bus system.

The county held 157,346 residents in 2020, and the Census Bureau estimates 157,556 for July 2025. The tenure split is close to even: the 2020 census counted exactly half of occupied homes as owner-occupied and half as rented, and the later survey puts owners at 51.4 percent. With about half of occupied homes rented, the owner on January 1, not the tenant, receives the tax statement.

sections.h2: When are Macon-Bibb property taxes billed and due?
sections.html:
Real and personal property statements go out by September 15. Bibb uses two installments: the first is due October 15 and the second November 15. A due date that falls on a weekend moves to the next business day.

The office bills the owner of record on January 1. If it learns about a transfer within 90 days of the due date, it bills the new owner once it verifies the change. Statements go to property owners, not mortgage companies, although the office does send each lender on record a data file listing amounts due. The owner stays responsible for making sure escrowed taxes actually get paid.

Mobile home statements are mailed by January 30 and are due April 1. A mobile home needs a current decal, issued when tax is paid. Late payment draws a state-mandated penalty of 10 percent of the tax or $5, whichever is greater, plus monthly interest.

sections.h2: How do I pay late or in installments in Macon-Bibb County?
sections.html:
The office accepts partial payments and lets you pay as many times as needed, but penalties and interest keep running on whatever remains. A U.S. Postal Service postmark counts as proof of an on-time payment on current-year tax, and a meter stamp does not. For delinquent accounts the office strongly urges paying in person, especially once a levy and tax sale advertisement have begun.

Before a FiFa lien is issued, the commissioner mails a 30-day notice of intent that gives you a chance to pay in full. A FiFa is recorded on the General Execution Docket at the Clerk of Superior Court, and the office says a lien can be filed when tax stays unpaid for more than 90 days after the due date. Paying the tax with the fees, penalties and interest cancels it. The office does not sell liens over the counter, and it says it does not report to credit bureaus.

The county also bills every residential premises, occupied or vacant, for garbage service through the Solid Waste Department, on a quarterly schedule. That fee serves a different purpose from the property tax, and if you appeal the value of your property the garbage fee is due in full anyway. Households under federal poverty guidelines can apply for an exemption by 5:00 p.m. on November 1 each year.

sections.h2: How does homestead exemption work in Macon-Bibb County?
sections.html:
The Tax Assessors approve homestead applications. You must own and occupy the house on January 1, and the application has to arrive before April 1 to count for that year. Once you are approved you do not reapply annually, but a move or a change to the deed means a new application.

Exemption amounts are set partly by state law and partly by local legislation, so the dollar figure on your bill is the one that counts. Ask the assessors at (478) 621-6701 what exemption your account carries and whether you qualify for any senior relief.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Macon-Bibb County value?
sections.html:
File a written appeal with the Board of Tax Assessors within 45 days of the notice date, and say which method of appeal you choose. The grounds can be taxability, value, uniformity or denial of an exemption. Appeal questions go to the assessors, and the Tax Commissioner is clear that it is an independent elected office that neither controls the assessors nor answers to them.

Mobile home owners follow a variant: appeal to the assessors within 45 days of the tax bill mailing or by April 1, whichever is later. State guidance gives all taxpayers three years from payment to claim a refund for tax that was erroneously or illegally collected.

sections.h2: What happens to a Macon-Bibb house with unpaid tax at a tax sale?
sections.html:
Once a FiFa exists, the property can be levied and sold. Sales are held on the first Tuesday of any month in which one is planned, at 11 a.m. on the courthouse steps at 206 7th Street, and bidders must be there in person. The opening bid is the tax plus penalties and fees, the winner receives a sheriff's tax deed and not the property itself, and payment is due within two hours in cash, certified funds or money orders.

The owner keeps a right of redemption. Georgia lets the owner or anyone with an interest redeem within 12 months of the sale, and the price can include the buyer's bid, taxes the buyer paid afterward, special assessments and a 20 percent premium. After 12 months the buyer may begin foreclosing that right through certified mail and four weeks of newspaper notice. Any surplus bid becomes excess funds that the office holds for lienholders first, then the record owner. Paying the tax out of sale proceeds before a levy keeps a house out of that process entirely.

faqs.q: What are the Macon-Bibb County property tax due dates?
faqs.a: October 15 for the first installment and November 15 for the second, with statements mailed by September 15. A weekend due date shifts to the next business day.

faqs.q: Does Macon-Bibb accept partial tax payments?
faqs.a: Yes, as many as you need. Interest and penalties keep accruing on the unpaid balance, and any balance can eventually be subject to a lien.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Macon-Bibb assessment?
faqs.a: 45 days from the date of the notice, filed in writing with the Board of Tax Assessors. Call (478) 621-6701 for appeal help.

faqs.q: Where can I get a copy of my Bibb County deed?
faqs.a: The Clerk of Superior Court deed room in the courthouse at 601 Mulberry Street, Macon, GA 31201, holds warranty deed copies.

faqs.q: Is a postmark accepted for Macon-Bibb tax payments?
faqs.a: Yes, a U.S. Postal Service dated postmark proves a timely current-year payment. Meter-dated postmarks do not count.
